title: University - BSc (Hons) First-Class Honours in Software Engineering
description: Growth begins the moment comfort ends
My Univeristy Years:

Life doesn’t always hand you clarity when you want it. Finishing my A-levels, I didn’t have some grand vision of who I wanted to become or what path I was destined to follow. Truthfully, my choices were influenced more by noise than conviction — teachers, friends and the constant hum of “tech is the future.”

My parents, on the other hand, had a far more traditional ambition for me. Medicine. Doctor. A noble path, just not my path. And perhaps it was that relentless push that nudged me further away. Combined with a fairly blasé attitude toward education at the time, I was a walking contradiction: capable of far more than I was willing to give. A foolish boy, in hindsight; But one about to learn an important lesson.
University became my reset button. A chance to turn things around.

I chose Software Engineering not from some lifelong passion, but because it felt… possible. My grades were good enough. The opportunity was there. Why not? And then something unexpected happened... I loved it.

What had once felt like “just another subject” suddenly clicked. I found myself genuinely curious. Engaged. Motivated. That spark changed everything. I applied myself fully and was rewarded with a First-class performance in my first year

Second year told a different story. I still worked hard, but I also lived; Probably a little too enthusiastically. Socialising, learning who I was, and developing confidence beyond the lecture theatre. The result? A 2:1. Respectable, but not what I wanted. I was disappointed and that discomfort mattered. It showed me I cared.
So when my final year arrived, I made a decision...
I committed. Fully!

The hours were long. The dedication intense. Even I surprised myself. My work, particularly in software testing, reflected that drive. I poured everything into my modules and dissertation; Even achieving a score of 95%+ in my Software Testing module, not just because I enjoyed it, but because I was determined to prove something to myself. I loved the discipline, the structure, the precision. It resonated deeply.

When results day came and I saw First-Class Honours, the pride I felt was unmatched. Not because of the title, but because I earned it. And because I could see, unmistakably, how proud my parents were. I hadn’t become a doctor, but I had become someone who followed through.
That moment became a core memory. One that will stay with me forever.
What It Set In Motion:

University taught me far more than software engineering. It taught me ownership. Discipline. Resilience. It showed me that progress doesn’t come from knowing, it comes from doing. From choosing effort over excuses. Growth over comfort.
Those lessons shaped everything that followed; How I work, how I lead and how I challenge myself to keep moving forward.

title: Barclaycard (Barclays)
description: This was where I really stopped learning in theory and started delivering in reality!
Scrum Master (Apr 2022 - Mar 2024):
- Led and coached 2 cross-functional application development teams delivering secure platforms within a regulated banking environment.
- Improved predictability to 80%+ and reduced backlog waste by 33% through stronger refinement, workflow discipline and realistic planning.
- Supported the organisation-wide move from Rally to Jira and trained teams on workflows, dashboards, JQL, board management and ticket hygiene.
- Took ownership of end-to-end testing for a JBoss 6 to JBoss 7 migration, coordinating testers from 8 teams and securing stakeholder sign-off.
- Worked with Product Owners, engineers, security and compliance teams to manage dependencies, implementation risk and operational readiness.
DevOps Engineer / Software Engineer (Jun 2018 - Apr 2022):
- Built and supported AWS-based platforms using Terraform, Jenkins, Chef, Packer, Ruby and OpenShift.
- Supported the migration of services from on-prem infrastructure to AWS, helping teams adopt new pipelines and cloud-based ways of working.
- Set up developer office hours and a support rota so teams had a clear route to raise issues, understand platform changes and request improvements.
- Worked across software engineering, infrastructure automation and CI/CD, building practical understanding of how application teams build, release and support services.

title: Discover Financial Services / Capital One
description: Fear of failure is the enemy of progress. To not do is to fail. So I choose to do. To try. To learn. To grow. And in doing so, I find success beyond measure!
Agile & Technical Programme Manager (Mar 2025 - Apr 2026):

- Led Agile delivery and programme execution across 7 engineering teams (~40+ engineers) within Discover's TRDC digital payments domain, supporting Capital One merger activity and multi-wave token migration readiness.

- Led complex digital payments and platform change across engineering, Product, architecture, risk and senior leadership with responsibility for roadmap alignment, dependencies, readiness and delivery outcomes.
- Took over a multi-wave token migration mid-flight, closed Wave 1 remediation items and built the governance, testing and operational readiness needed for Wave 2.

- Set up a scalable delivery model across 7 teams by standardising PI planning, refinement, capacity planning, release coordination and escalation routes so teams could operate with less day-to-day support.
- Created process flowcharts and practical guidance for Product Owners and teams covering refinement, epic readiness and stronger story writing.
- Improved delivery predictability from 65% to 85%, reduced epic cycle time from 100+ days to ~55 days and increased backlog maturity to 2+ months of delivery-ready work.
- Challenged outdated performance data for higher migration volumes and drove renewed API stress testing and end-to-end validation to uncover degradation and timeout risks.
- Produced evidence-based scalability assessments for senior engineering leadership and Capital One partners, comparing expected migration demand against platform capability.
- Coordinated the resolution of cross-system response mapping defects affecting digital wallet and tokenisation services, aligning remediation, testing and controlled production sign-off.
- Designed and facilitated migration game-day plans covering pre-migration, go-dark and post-migration validation, identifying missing scenarios before implementation.
- Maintained RAID governance and provided clear updates on risks, timelines, dependencies and decisions across technical teams and senior leadership.
Scrum Master (Mar 2024 - Mar 2025):
- Coached distributed engineering teams across the UK and India, helping them improve self-organisation, ownership and delivery discipline.
- Redesigned refinement from live group story writing into a clearer epic-to-story process, increasing engagement and building 2 to 3 months of ready backlog.
- Introduced delivery dashboards and regular reviews covering predictability, cycle time, bottlenecks and work in progress to support evidence-based improvement.
- Built a capacity planner using team availability and historical delivery rates, helping teams make more realistic sprint and PI commitments.
- Acted as Product Owner proxy during coverage gaps, maintaining prioritisation, backlog clarity and delivery continuity.
- Facilitated no-blame retrospectives and post-mortems including a cross-location Kafka review that led to improved cycle time and collaboration.

title: Career Break
description: Taking time to travel, recharge and enjoy the freedom to choose what comes next.
Current status:
After completing my time with Discover Financial Services / Capital One in April 2026, I chose to step away from full-time work and take a proper career break.

I am currently travelling, enjoying life and exploring what I want the next chapter to look like. That could mean the right permanent opportunity, contract work, or building a business of my own—but I am in no rush to choose a path simply for the sake of returning to work.
For now, the focus is on new experiences, personal projects and making the most of the freedom to decide what comes next.
